# Zotero PDF batch mode

Discovery summaries are abstract-based. To summarize **full PDFs** already in
your Zotero library, use `--zotero-collection`.

## Finding your collection path

The path is the one shown in Zotero's collection tree, not the random
`~/Zotero/storage/...` folder name. For a library that looks like this in
Zotero's sidebar:

```text
My Library
├── Reading
│   ├── Deep Reading          →  --zotero-collection 'Reading/Deep Reading'
│   └── Skimmed               →  --zotero-collection 'Reading/Skimmed'
├── Writing
│   └── CHI 2027 submission   →  --zotero-collection 'Writing/CHI 2027 submission'
└── Inbox                     →  --zotero-collection 'Inbox'
```

Ask PaperTracker rather than transcribing by hand:

```bash
uv run papertracker --list-zotero-collections
```

If two collections share a leaf name, use the full path. An optional
`My Library/` prefix is accepted and ignored.

Zotero's data directory is `~/Zotero` by default on macOS, Linux, and Windows
alike — it holds `zotero.sqlite` and `storage/`. Point
`PAPERTRACKER_ZOTERO_DIR` elsewhere if you moved it; Zotero's own
[data directory guide](https://www.zotero.org/support/zotero_data) shows where
to check. Running PaperTracker under WSL against a Zotero installed on Windows
counts as moved: reach it through the mount, as
`PAPERTRACKER_ZOTERO_DIR=/mnt/c/Users/<you>/Zotero`.

## Quoting the name

Every example here uses **single** quotes. Zotero allows characters in a
collection name that a shell reads as syntax, and the one that bites is `!`:
inside *double* quotes, bash and zsh treat it as a history reference and the
command dies before PaperTracker ever starts.

```text
$ uv run papertracker --zotero-collection "!Projects/To Read"
bash: !Projects/To: event not found
```

Single quotes pass the name through literally — `!`, `&`, `$`, and spaces alike.
Nothing about this is PaperTracker-specific, so no flag or config key changes it:

- **bash, zsh** (macOS, Linux, WSL) — use single quotes. `set +H` turns history
  expansion off for the session if you would rather keep double quotes.
- **PowerShell** — either quote style works; it has no history expansion.
- **cmd.exe** — use double quotes. It has no history expansion either, and it
  does not treat single quotes as delimiters, so they would end up inside the
  collection name.

## Running it

```bash
uv run papertracker --list-zotero-collections
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection 'Reading/Deep Reading'
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection 'Reading/Deep Reading' --template deep-human-study
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection 'Reading/Deep Reading' --select
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection 'Reading/Deep Reading' --zotero-include-subcollections
```

For both Claude and Codex, PaperTracker extracts text locally, preserves page
labels, processes every extractable page in bounded chunks, recursively
consolidates notes when needed, and only then fills the selected template. A
missing or image-only PDF fails before an LLM call with an `OCR required`
message; partially extractable PDFs continue with a warning.

Output lands in `user_data/digests/<project-id>/zotero/<collection-slug>/`,
where the slug is the collection path lowercased with every run of
non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-` — so `'Reading/Deep Reading'` writes
to `zotero/reading-deep-reading/`.

Because these are full-text runs, use a `fulltext` template — see
[Summary templates](templates.md#writing-one).

## Your library is never modified

The Zotero database is opened **read-only**: PaperTracker copies
`zotero.sqlite` to a temporary file first, then opens that copy with SQLite's
`mode=ro`. Zotero holds a lock on the live database while it runs, and the copy
is what makes the read safe. Nothing is written back, and the temporary copy is
deleted when the run ends.

This is the approach Zotero itself prescribes for third-party tools — see
[direct SQLite access](https://www.zotero.org/support/dev/client_coding/direct_sqlite_database_access),
which asks that external readers never touch the live file.
